utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Tecla Henry-Benjamin and Daryl Mundis. We are assisted today by our case manager, Skye Winner. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel, and Alexis Demirdjian, our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for the other Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present, the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in the courtroom, and I would like to mention our legal officer in particular, who has left us and should soon be replaced. In the meantime, we will continue with our work. We have a witness scheduled for today. But before we call the witness into the courtroom, I would like to address the Defence about the issue of two revisions that we have asked the translation service to do. On the 22nd of December, we asked CLSS to inform us of the translation of DH165. CLSS told us that having examined the document, they were of the opinion that the translation was correct. The Defence objected or said that they would provide us with other clarifications. For the moment, I haven't received any such clarifications, but we are waiting for Defence counsel to tell us in what respect CLSS has mistranslated the section in question. On the 13th of January, we also requested another translation. We wanted to know whether the 30 Arab soldiers were with or behind the 7th Muslim Brigade. The translation department sent us a memo dated the 13th of January saying that it was possible to interpret this passage in two manners and that one might also interpret the passages meaning that the Arabs were behind the 7th Brigade in the relevant area. So you have certainly received this memo. Is there anything that any of the parties would like to comment on with regard to the memo? Mr. Dixon, I believe that you would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In respect of the Exhibit 4, Mr. Hadzihasanovic, that's document 1360, about whether the Arab soldiers were left behind by the 7th Muslim Brigade or after the 7th Muslim Brigade left the area, Your Honour, we have studied the same document that came from the Translation Unit. It appears, as Your Honour has correctly said, that the matter can be looked at either way. This is somewhat confusing to us because in our view, certainly looking at it with the English translation in mind, the meaning is very different from the one translation to the next. There are certainly significant differences in the two meanings. And we would have expected that that would have, in the translation, been made clear as well. In our submission, the correct way of reviewing that particular passage is that the 30 Arab soldiers remained behind after the 7th Muslim Brigade left this area and that that is the interpretation which we would submit should be given to this passage. Your Honours, we would request that if necessary, if this is a significant matter that, further inquiry be made in order to resolve this matter, as it may be one of some significance. In addition, Your Honours, we, as the Defence, would also be in a position to provide a independent translation of that passage should that be necessary to seek to resolve the matter and to support our submission that the correct interpretation is that these Arab soldiers were there remaining behind after the 7th Brigade left this area. Your Honour -- Your Honour, if I may add one further matter: The other point which should be taken into account when assessing this matter is that the witness himself who prepared this document and who gave testimony in this respect has confirmed in his testimony - and I can find the relevant page - that the interpretation, which is correct, is the one that the 7th Brigade was there remaining behind after the 30 Arab soldiers had left, but that was the -- the way in which this situation unfolded, and in our submission his account would accord with what is recorded in the document if the interpretation that we submit is correct is given to -- to that document. Sorry, Your Honour, there's one problem with the translation again, and that is that the 7th Brigade had left this area and -- and not the Arab soldiers. That's in line 5 on page 4. Sorry, in our submission, Your Honour, what the witness said in his testimony accords with what we say is the correct interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The translation we have in English is not satisfactory because the first translation states that the small unit of Arabs consisting of 30 soldiers "left behind by." This means that the 7th left them behind because we have the preposition "by." One has the impression that this small unit was left behind by the 7th Brigade. And the English continues and it states "which has left this area." Maybe the 7th Brigade left the area. The translation gives the impression that this unit was left behind by the 7th Brigade, which had apparently left the area. The second translation omits the term "by" and says: "All remained behind the 7th Brigade," et cetera. So it's not very clear. And I believe that it is necessary to ask CLSS to provide us with a precise response. There are two essential issues at stake here: Was this unit left behind by the 7th Brigade, and did it remain behind the position of the 7th Brigade? Because the key issue is the term "by" the 7th Brigade. Are there any linguistic comment that the Prosecution would like to make about the matter? Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution would have no objection to the Trial Chamber again querying CLSS on this specific. It appears however that the memo that we've received has clearly indicated that it found the translation to be correct, although there is an alternate way of rendering the text, which is what the memo says. It appears as though the way the bracketed text is set forth in both the correct version and the alternate version, it seems to us to be really a reflection of the passive use of the language versus a more active use of the English language, but again we would have no objection to CLSS being asked again to attempt to clarify this for us. We -- and this may be premature at this point, but we would certainly like to be heard before any kind of independent translation is again taking of this. Our view is that CLSS within the registry here is in fact an independent translation service and it's an excellent one. And before the parties go out seeking to have, in brackets, independent translations done of document, we would certainly like to be heard before that course is taken. But we certainly have no objection to CLSS being asked very specifically to clarify this point. Although, again, in our submission, it seems to us that it's quite clear they have said the translation is correct; however, there is an alternative way of rendering this text, and the difference it Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond seems to us is one in which in the -- in the first version, it's a very active voice; and in the second version, it's simply a passive voice. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, CLSS should translate the B/C/S text into French. So we should have a translation from B/C/S into French. And then a translation of B/C/S into English. And this will enable us to compare the two translations. This should shed a little more light on -- on the issue. But it's necessary to have a direct translation from B/C/S into French so that we can make a comparison. We'll address this issue again once this matter has been dealt with. As far as the other document is concerned, D165, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good day, Mr. President. Good day, Your Honours. As far as DH165 is concerned, the difficulty, Mr. President, is that we don't know exactly which part of the sentence was confirmed by CLSS. When their reply arrived, they said that they were confirming the translation but didn't specify the exact part concerned. In addition, we have the same document that was translated into French in another case, and the result was quite different from the English translation. So we have a French version and we have an English version and a B/C/S version. It's necessary to take additional steps to have this document confirmed. As far as we are concerned - and if necessary, we'll ask for a final verification by the CLSS - but as far as we are concerned, we are trying to obtain such confirmation of the relevant passage. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As far as the first document is concerned, we are on standby now and we'll wait for more information before we render our decision. There's also another decision that had to be rendered about a document that the Prosecution objected to. We will inform you of our decision after the break. Without wasting any more time, we will now call the witness scheduled for today into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir. I would first like to make sure that you are receiving the interpretation of what I am saying. If so, please confirm the fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day. And yes, I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have been called here as a witness for Defence counsel for one of the accused. Before you take the solemn declaration, I would be grateful if you could tell me your first and last names, your date of birth, and your place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Mirsad Ibrakovic. I was born on the 1st of January, 1950 in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Are you currently employed? And if so, what sort of position do you hold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am employed. I work in the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You work in the Ministry of Defence. Are you employed there in a military capacity? If so, what is your rank and what sort of assignment do you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a state functionary. And the rank I have is that of a reserve brigadier. But I don't work as a member of the military. I work as a state official. At the moment, I work as the chief of the Department for Defence in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 and 1993, did you hold a position of any kind in your country? And if you were a member of the military, which unit were you in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was employed in the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence in Zenica, and I was the chief of the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You remained in the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence in Zenica. Were you assigned to an ABiH unit at some subsequent date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the Municipal Territorial Defence -- when the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff in Zenica was disbanded, I went to the 33rd Light Brigade [as interpreted], a newly formed brigade, where I was appointed the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You were the commander of the 33rd Brigade. The 33rd Brigade, because according to the transcript it says "the 33rd Brigade."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the 330th Light Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 330th. Very well. There is an error in the transcript in that case. Three-three-zero. Very well. Should I call you, sir, by general? How would you like called? Mr. Ibrakovic or general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. or sir is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, have you already testified before a national or international court about the events that took place in your country, or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never testified before. This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to Defence counsel, I would like to provide you with some information about the procedure that we will be following here. As you know, you will be testifying here at the request of the Defence. Defence counsel for one of the accused at your left, and you have already met them before coming here, and you will have to answer a series of questions that we'll put to you. The questions put to you should be put in neutral terms. They should not be leading. You will be asked to answer the question. Defence counsel shouldn't try to put words into your mouth. Once this has -- once this stage has been completed, the Prosecution, who are to your right, will ask you questions, but the questions put to you in the course of their cross-examination will be different from the ones put to you by Defence counsel. Defence counsel may not put leading questions to you; however, the party that cross-examines a witness may put leading questions to the witness. For example, they might say: Would you agree with me if I said such and such a thing. And then you will either agree or you won't agree. So the questions put to you in the course of the cross-examination will be somewhat different. This is perhaps a little complicated, but I wanted to inform you of the fact. Once this stage has been completed, Defence counsel may ask you additional questions, if they wish to do so, but these questions will be directly related to the questions put to you by the Prosecution. Defence counsel and the Prosecution may also show you documents to ask you to comment on them. Usually these documents are documents of a military kind. The three Judges sitting before you may ask you questions at any point in time, according to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, but usually the Judges prefer to wait for the parties to have completed their examination before intervening. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond If it seems that it's important to clarify an issue, in such a case the Judges might ask the witness a question. According to the Rules, the Judges are allowed to put any type of question to witnesses. There are no limits. This is what the Rules provide for. As a rule, the Judges ask questions to clarify a witness's testimony or because they believe that it would be in the interest of justice to ask a witness to confirm, for example, something stated by the Defence. We might also use some of the documents presented to you or some of the documents that have already been admitted into evidence. Because in addition to verifying the substance of your testimony, the Judges might feel it necessary to verify the credibility of a witness. Generally speaking, this is the procedure we'll be following, but there are two other points I need to mention: You have taken the solemn declaration and you have said you will be speaking the truth, which means that you should not give false testimony. False testimony given before this Tribunal is an offence and a prison sentence of up to seven years could be given to a witness for false testimony. As you have taken the solemn declaration, you are obliged to tell the truth. In addition, when a witness is asked to answer a question, he may refuse to answer the question if the witness believes that his answer could be used against him. In such a case, the Chamber can compel the witness to answer the question, but the Chamber grants the witness a form of immunity. I wanted to point this out to you. If you feel that a question is complicated, ask the person putting the question to you to rephrase it. You will be asked about events that took place over ten years ago, and perhaps you can't remember everything or perhaps you won't understand a question, so ask the person putting the question to you to rephrase it. In such a case, try to be as concise and clear as possible. We don't have any written documents concerning your testimony. I have just found out that you were the commander of the 330th Brigade. But that's only because this is something that you have stated. I don't know what sort of questions you will be asked and I don't know what sort of answers you will be providing. As you will see, there is a screen before you, and you will be able to follow your answers transcribed in English on the screen. If you feel the need to ask any questions, don't hesitate to do so. We are here to answer any questions you might have. Your hearing should take up part of the afternoon, but this is the information I wanted to provide you with before giving the floor to Defence counsel, who will now commence with the examination-in-chief. Defence counsel will be putting non-leading questions to you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Ms. Residovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Ibrakovic.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the important information the Presiding Judge has just provided you with, there is something else I would like to point out to you. When you hear my question, please pause briefly so that the interpreters have time to interpret the question, and then you can answer the question. This will enable the Chamber and my colleagues in the courtroom to follow our exchanges. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Ibrakovic, what is your profession and what was your education before the war?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: By profession I am a teacher. I obtained my university degree at the Faculty of Political Sciences in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, before the war, did you serve in the army and did you hold any rank?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before the war, I served in the JNA in the reserve officers school in Bileca, and before the beginning of the war I was deployed in the Territorial Defence and my rank was that of reserve major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When asked by the President, you said that when the war started and during 1992 and 1993 you were the chief of the Municipal Territorial Staff of Zenica -- Territorial Defence Staff. Mr. Ibrakovic, was this the duty you were performing on the 6th of April when Bosnia and Herzegovina was attacked?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was employed in the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff. And when the aggression started, I was holding that post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the commanders of the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the Municipal Staff was Jozo Jerkic, whom I found in the staff. And until he was wounded sometime in May, he was the commander of the staff. In May, a new commander was appointed, Mr. Branko Boncina, who had been a commander previously but he had retired. However, as the then-commander, Jozo Jerkic had been wounded. The wartime president of Zenica Municipality appointed Branko Boncina commander. He was commander until about the month of October or November, when Jasmin Saric was appointed commander. Jasmin Saric remained the commander until the staff was disbanded in 1993. So these were the three commanders in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just told us that one of the commanders was appointed by the wartime presidency. Tell us: In 1992, who appointed the commanders of the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: It's like this: Pursuant to the then-law on All People's Defence, which had been enacted in 1974, the commander of the Municipal Staff was appointed by the municipal assembly with a previous approval of the commander of the Republican Territorial Defence Staff. Within that legal framework, Jozo Jerkic was appointed command. After he was wounded, the role was taken over by the wartime Presidency and the Crisis Staff of the municipality, and they took on all the powers that the municipal assembly had had. With the previous approval of, I think, the then-commander of the District Staff, the wartime Presidency appointed Branko Boncina commander. So they were taking on the role of the assembly. And that's what happened with the commander who was appointed after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask before I continue my examination that a set of documents be shown to the witness. We have a sufficient number of copies for Your Honours, and I must apologise, Your Honours, due to the well-known translation problem, there is a significant number of documents pertaining to the work of the TO that -- in the relevant period that has not been translated in 1992. We shall submit the translations as soon as we receive them from CLSS so that we shall now act on your suggestion and show the witness the documents and ask him to tell us what they are about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, you said that when the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina started, you started applying the then-law of the SFRY on All People's Defence. And I am now asking you whether the organs in Zenica in the first half or, rather, in what period of 1992 did they implement the previous law on All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I have to correct you. It was not the law of All People's Defence of the SFRY. It was the law on All People's Defence of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That was the law that was valid for us; although, of course, it had been brought into line with the law of the SFRY of the time. However, this was the law that was in force. And because I had been employed in the TO staff previously - "TO" means "Territorial Defence," of course - I was familiar with the law because I had implemented it in peacetime. When the aggression on Bosnia and Herzegovina started, the law was still valid and we implemented it for quite a long time. In the beginning, in the initial confusion, it was the basis on which we acted. And I think until the autumn of 1992, we worked in compliance as far as we were able to with that law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said "until the autumn." In the autumn, did you get new legislation from Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted in May of the same year?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: We had certain information that a change of the legislation was Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond about to take place, but it was rather late that we received this legislation. I don't know why it was not sent on to us at once, why it wasn't available to us right away, but we received it quite late.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you now look at the document in Roman I, 0409, that's the first document in the bundle, and would you please read what organ issued this document, its number and date, and tell me what this is actually about.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a conclusion of the Council for National Defence of the Municipality of Zenica. Your Honours, you may know that the way the work of the assembly was organised: There was an advisory body of the municipal assembly and this was the Council for National Defence or the National Defence Council. And important people from the municipality were on that council, including a representative of the JNA barracks, a representative of the TO and of the Secretariat of Defence. These were the military structures represented. There was also the president of the Municipality, the president of the Municipal Executive Council. And at this meeting on the 7th of June, they reached a conclusion on the mobilisation of the complete TO force at the disposal of the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff in accordance with the valid defence plans that had been drawn up in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just wanted to indicate clearly for Their Honours what this document is about because unfortunately it has no translation. Would you now, please, look at document number 2 and tell us when it was enacted and what this is about. It's Defence number 1652.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 1 has a translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 2 has no translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read the title of the document, when it was issued, and by whom, and tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: As this was still in the early stages, when Zenica had not yet been attacked directly, the Municipal Assembly of Zenica in its full numbers, pursuant to the Statute of the Municipality, Article 293, item 2, regulated that during an imminent threat of war or during a war a Crisis Staff should be established. On the basis of the statutory decision, the municipal assembly reached a decision on forming a Crisis Staff of Zenica municipality, which would include a certain number of civil servants holding posts in the municipality in various areas, such as defence, security, the police, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, would you now please look at the document numbered "3," Defence number 1654. And this has no translation either, so would you please read the preamble, the title of the document, and then I will ask you just to read some parts of the document and respond to some questions about it. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The previous document regulated the formation of the Crisis Staff. The Crisis Staff issued its own documents on its work, and pursuant to this decision, sessions were scheduled. This document reads as follows: "Pursuant to Article 1 of the decision on the forming of a Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Zenica, the Crisis Staff of the Municipality at its third session, held on the 11th of April, 1992, hereby makes the following conclusions." And there is a list of conclusions here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please read paragraph 1 and paragraph 3 and paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it says: "The already-existing armed forces on the ground should be put under the control of the Territorial Defence and mobilisation should be carried out." Item 3: "In order to expand the Crisis Staff and to have the following become permanent members, Mirsad Mesic, commander of the municipal TO staff, and Dizdar Dzevad, the secretary of the Municipal Secretariat for the Economy and Finance."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 reads as follows: "The TO Staff is to be put into a state of full combat readiness with the focus on forming new units and their arming."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, this newly established Territorial Defence Staff and wartime presidency of the Municipality of Zenica which took on the functions of the assembly, in accordance with their position under the previous law on All People's Defence, are they now taking on certain duties and responsibilities in relation to the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff and what was their role?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You see, according to the law on All People's Defence, even previously, the municipal assembly formed the staff, regulated its organisation and formation, appointed the commander, and the commander according to these provisions was responsible both to the Municipal Assembly of Zenica and now, as the Crisis Staff, it felt that it had certain competencies in assigning tasks. And we received these tasks and carried them out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now, please, look at the document in tab 5, 1656 is the number of the document. Again, there is no translation. So would you please read the preamble and the title of the document and tell us briefly, if you can, what this document indicates.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 1 of the decision on the forming of the Crisis Staff of Zenica municipality, the Crisis Staff of the municipality at its eighth session, held on the 13th of April, adopts the following conclusion."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at conclusion number 3 and tell us what the Crisis Staff is trying to do here.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Conclusion number 3: "The Crisis Staff of Zenica municipality, the security forces, and the Territorial Defence guarantee to citizens of all nationalities, Muslims, Serbs, Croats, and members of other nations, safety and security on the territory of the Municipality of Zenica." This is dated the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, as you were employed in the Municipal TO Staff before the beginning of the war and continued in April during the war, when the municipality took over its wartime duties, tell me, at that time, did you carry out a certain mobilisation and according to what rules and regulations did you do so in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: It's like this: Of course we had the task in peacetime of organising the Territorial Defence, of preparing it, training it, equipping it, and using it in certain situations according to plans we drew up at the time and according to the doctrine of the superior commands. These plans existed in case there was a war, in case there was an aggression, but not this kind of aggression that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the document under tab 7, 0393. This document does have a translation. Could you please tell me what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want me to read or just comment?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, just comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as we already had a certain Territorial Defence that had been established and certain existing units, units which were to be mobilised in a situation like the one which arose, and we had received the order from the Crisis Staff to mobilise these units, this is a report submitted to the superior command on the mobilisation of these units, which had been carried out, the number of men who responded and the situation after the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at document number 8. It's 1658, a Defence number. It has no translation. And you will read only the preamble, the conclusion, and paragraph 1, and please tell me whether this is in fact a document corroborating your testimony to the effect that the Crisis Staff was now giving its approval, issuing orders for mobilisation, and the creation of new Territorial Defence units.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this decision, to form a Crisis Staff, the Crisis Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond Staff of the Municipality of Zenica at its 11th session, held on the 16th of April, adopted a conclusion. "The proposal made by the TO Staff to form new TO units is hereby accepted, and leave is given for the TO Staff to take decisions on mobilising Territorial Defence units." And I'll emphasise again that forming TO units -- that the assembly is giving leave for the formation of TO units. The municipal assembly made such a proposal. The commander of the Municipal Staff on the basis of such a decision at the time believed that it was necessary to mobilise new units. This was accepted by the municipal assembly -- or rather, the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Read conclusion 3, and could you read that through. Is that also one of the rules that was necessary to respect?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "It's necessary to urgently form a military police unit which will control members of TO units in cooperation with the MUP." I wouldn't say that this was the competence of the municipal assembly and the assembly according to the law at the time, but given the situation and the fact that there were a lot of armed individuals and groups in the town, it was necessary to establish order to the extent this was possible and it was necessary to form adequate MP, military police units. We had a detachment of ten men, and this was not sufficient to deal with all the work. This is probably why this conclusion was adopted and afterwards we formed a large MP unit of 30 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document 9. 1659 is the number. We don't have a translation of the document. But tell me what the heading, the title of the document is, and tell me what this document represents.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: 1659; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "On the basis of a decision of the Presidency on declaring an imminent threat of war and pursuant to Article 1 of the decision on forming a Crisis Staff in the Municipality of Zenica, the Crisis Staff of the municipality at a session -- at the twentieth session held on the 22nd of April, 1992 adopted the following order on introducing a curfew in the territory of the Municipality of Zenica. "A curfew is hereby introduced in the Municipality of Zenica from 2400 hours to 0500 hours. The public security station in Zenica will be responsible for carrying out this order."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have just said, that the Crisis Staff started taking certain decisions because of the overall situation and the armed individuals present in the area, have a look at document number 11, 1660. We don't have a translation of this document either. And could you tell me what this conclusion relates to.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Should I read it out?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "On the basis of Article 1 of the decision on forming a Crisis Staff in the Municipality of Zenica, the Crisis Staff of the municipality at the 24th session held on the 1st of May, 1992 hereby adopts the following conclusion: The commander of the regional TO Staff is hereby made responsible to deal with the relationship, with members of the Busovaca TO -- or, rather, to investigate the movement of armed individuals in the territory of the Municipality of Zenica and must take the necessary measures if they have been moving around without authorisation."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, we have heard that a region consists of a lot of municipalities, so tell me, how is it that the Crisis Staff is now taking over this role? It's also issuing orders to an organ that is superior to it. What were the conditions in Zenica at the time that made it necessary for such things to occur as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this doesn't seem to be quite logical, but the situation in the field was far more complex. The Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Zenica met on a daily basis, had sessions on a daily basis; whereas, the region that was responsible for a number of municipalities wasn't fully staffed. There were few members. They probably couldn't follow the entire situation. But since there were armed individuals from other municipalities, in particular in Busovaca, who were in Zenica - that's where they would cause certain problems - since this was the case, the Crisis Staff at its session, when it examined the political and security situation in the town, made the Regional TO Staff responsible to introduce order, to deal with the situation. I assume that that is what is -- what happened, because this is the first time I've seen the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at document number 22. 1673 is the number of the document. We don't have a -- an English version of the document either.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a document from the War Presidency of the Crisis Staff. Could you please read out the preamble and the first paragraph and the name listed under number 2.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 1 on the decision of forming a War Presidency of the Crisis Staff of Zenica municipality, Official Gazette such and such a number, the War Presidency at the session held on the 20th of October 1992, having examined the political and security situation in the territory of the Municipality of Zenica adopted the following conclusion: In order to put an end to hostilities in the territory of the municipality Novi Travnik and Vitez, a working group composed of the following member will hereby be formed. Under number 2 it says Dzemal Merdan, commander of the army regional staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, do the two document that is you have just had a look at show that in fact in 1992 the Crisis Staff of Zenica municipality was in fact the body that dealt with all the problems that arose, regardless of what its specific role in fact was, because the conditions were such that it was necessary to proceed in this manner?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In normal conditions, would it be possible for the president of the municipality to issue orders to the commander of a regional staff who is in a totally different position in -- from a military point of view and could he give orders to someone who had responsibilities that had nothing to do with the Zenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, this wouldn't have occurred. But given the events in the surroundings, the Zenica was also affected. There was pressure on the town of Zenica. And when we tried to find solution -- well, they probably weren't doing what they were in fact responsible for, but in such cases people do everything they can to improve the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 12, please. It hasn't been translated. 1662 is the number, and could you please read out the preamble and the first, second, and third conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 1 of the decision on forming a Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Zenica, the Crisis Staff of the municipality at its 44th session, held on the 17th of May, 1992, in order to withdraw from the Josip Jovanovic barracks in safety and unhindered, the following conclusion was adopted: Number one, the Crisis Staffs in local communes in the territory of Zenica must not take any measures or any steps without the Crisis Staff of Zenica municipality having issued orders and instructions. Conclusion number 2 or item number 1: Crisis Staffs in local communes are hereby ordered not to interfere in the command and control of TO units present in their area." Conclusion 3: "All armed groups and units in the territory of certain local communes that are not under the command of the TO and the MUP must be placed under the command of the Crisis Staff of the relevant local commune."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, since we have read out some conclusions of the Crisis Staff from April to October, could you tell me who had real power in Zenica, who took certain measures in terms of defence, who had civilian authority. So who in fact had real power and whose orders and instructions did you in fact carry out?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of everything that we have seen here, it is quite Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond clear that the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency in Zenica municipality were the bodies that took very important and essential decisions, and these bodies in fact had real power in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, could you please tell me what the overall situation was like in Zenica in 1992. What sort of issues was the town of Zenica confronted with during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see in this introduction, Zenica soon organised itself -- organised itself for a pre-war crisis situation, so to speak. It established a certain number of bodies so it were in a position to govern the town. Naturally, in the territory of the municipality. Of course, the town also faced a number of other problems because many of the bodies, many of the institutions had been damaged. They were ineffective. People had left. All the bodies had in a certain sense been truncated, but new -- new staff were recruited in order to ensure that all these institutions functioned properly. In certain cases, this proceeded smoothly; in other cases, not so smoothly. But in any event, an attempt was made to ensure that the town would not suffer the sort of fighting or sort of war that other towns in the vicinity had had to go through. So such measures were taken, but there was a lot of pressure. A lot of refugees arrived. And in a certain sense these people saw that there was some form of security in Zenica. There were many refugees from those areas, in particular from Krajina and from Eastern Bosnia, and they found refuge in Zenica, and this was a problem that compounded the difficulties we were faced with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, given that there were so many refugees, given the wartime conditions, were military units being formed in addition to the mobilisation that you carried out in the Territorial Defence, were various military units also established? If so, what sort of units were established and what was their attitude towards the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, this was the most serious problem that the Municipal Staff had to confront at the time. Above all, the Municipal Staff was organised -- or rather, a new form of the TO was organised and certain changes were made in the TO in Sarajevo, as far as we know. A lot of pressure was exerted on the staff itself. People wanted to arm themselves. They wanted units to be organised. Because companies weren't really functioning properly. The people were afraid. They wanted security by organising units -- by establishing units. Naturally, we mobilised units that had been prepared according to plans. And in addition to those TO units, to our units -- I say "our units," because the TO at the time was the only legitimate force. In addition to those units, other units were formed. They did this on their own initiative and certain political potentates and political parties formed such units. There were a number of such groups, a number of such units, and we all tried to place these units under unified TO command, and we received orders from our superior command according to which we were to place all these units under a single command. At the time in Zenica, in addition to the Territorial Defence, there was the HVO, there was the HOS - the Croatian Defence forces - there was the Patriotic League, and naturally the Territorial Defence, and then there were many other formations that had come from other areas and were present in the territory of the Municipality of Zenica. So there was a collection of such units and we tried to place all these units under a single command. In April and May, the work we had to carry out in this respect was very intensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you mentioned the HVO, the HOS, and the Patriotic League, were these formations placed under the command -- or, rather, did they become part of the Territorial Defence? That's my first question. And the second question is whether they were placed under the command of your Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I have already said, there were negotiations. Agreements were made. And on the basis of the order from the regional staff, by the 15th of April they had formally joined the TO but they had set certain conditions. Formally they had joined the Territorial Defence but they were not under the Territorial Defence's de facto command. This caused me significant problems. But they did join the Territorial Defence Staff because of their logistical needs on the whole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Since you have mentioned the formation of numerous other units, how many armed formations were there in Zenica in 1992 at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first there were five or six and then another five. Then they started forming new units in labour organisations and in local communes in accordance with the -- the law that made this possible. Units were formed in local communes and in labour organisations. They then started forming groups where it wasn't that necessary but groups were formed because people were afraid that they would be attacked in certain places. So the number of groups and units formed continued to increase. I remember a report we sent to the Regional Staff according to which there were 127 different units which had formally joined the Territorial Defence. These were units from detachments, to companies, to platoons, to groups. The 127th unit was a TV unit, and their task was to provide security for the television companies at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's not dwell on these problems any longer because I think that Their Honours have already heard about this difficult situation. Tell me, how would you describe the situation from the aspect of military organisation in Zenica in early November when Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic arrived there with the task of reorganising all the forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The situation in Zenica was critical. Seen from the viewpoint of the tasks of accommodating and feeding the refugees and the local population, the situation was very difficult and very chaotic. This is what the wartime Presidency was dealing with. I was dealing with the organisation and the security for the various facilities in the municipality, but this was beyond our capacity to ensure because so many people were arriving. They all wanted to join TO units, at first because they wanted to get cigarettes or salaries or because they wanted to get weapons so they could defend their homes, and it grew to the number I've mentioned. And this became unmanageable. It was impossible to keep all this under control. You couldn't have 127 different units, so we welcomed the news that there would be a reorganisation, that a military structure would be imposed, and I was glad to hear that this team, headed by Mr. Hadzihasanovic, was arriving. I felt a great sense of relief because somebody with knowledge and with authority was arriving who would be able to solve this. We didn't need that number of units in Zenica at the time. The process was difficult. It was very hard to bring them all into line, because they were already there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely what my next question was going to be. Through the decisions you have read out, we saw that real control over the Municipal Staff and other units was exerted by the wartime Presidency. 127 different armed units were recorded by you alone. What was the task now facing Enver Hadzihasanovic when he had to take over authority from all these various commanders and draw a distinction, a dividing line, between military and civilian authorities? Were you a witness of all the problems that the 3rd Corps faced when it was being established?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, I was relieved. We needed someone with authority to come along, someone who was not burdened with local politics, who could not be influenced by local politicians, because we were all local people and we came under the influence of local politicians since we lived there. And, of course, Mr. Hadzihasanovic was welcomed by some of the officers who knew what the problems were. I myself was very enthusiastic. However, there were others who were not enthusiastic at all, who didn't want law and order to be imposed, who profited from this kind of situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, tell me, what happened to the HVO? Did they accept the command of the 3rd Corps? Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The HVO was always playing a double game. From the very beginning, they had their own organisation and they gladly joined the Territorial Defence in March or April because, when the JNA left the barracks in Zenica, we had our TO depots there with quite a lot of weapons and ammunition and other equipment. They joined the Territorial Defence in order to get as much of this as possible for themselves, and they always paid lip service. But when we had to secure a facility -- we had 150 facilities on the territory of the municipality which had to be guarded in crisis situations and we didn't have enough weapons. We protected only 50 of these. And the HVO refused to abide by any of the previous decisions. They did not agree that, for example, a certain transformer station or something had to be guarded, that it was of significance for the municipality. They always did as they pleased, and they never de facto accepted the command of the TO. And as far as I know, the same happened with the 3rd Corps, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a brigade formed outside the Army of BH?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: This brigade in Zenica I believe was formed by people from Vitez. When Zivko Totic arrived as HVO commander in Zenica - he was probably sent by the operations command in Vitez with a task of establishing a brigade - in the autumn -- in October, but I'm not sure precisely -- they set themselves apart from the TO. They no longer needed its logistical support. They had got what they wanted from it. And now they were receiving logistical support from Vitez. They established the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there when this brigade was formed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: As we had certain orders that there should not be a conflict in Zenica and that all the minor incidents that took place from day to day should be solved so as not to escalate into a conflict, we cooperated quite well with the HVO commander, Zoran Covic, who was there initially. And later on, when Zivko Totic arrived, as he had been born in Zenica municipality, we continued our cooperation. I cannot recall now whether he invited us to the first line-up of the brigade or whether we went there purely out of curiosity, to see it. We were not in any special place of honour. We just stood to one side and observed the ceremony of the lining-up of the brigade and the speeches made by the guests.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does anything stick in your memory?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. After the official line-up and the initial ceremony, speeches were made. And when Mr. -- his name escapes me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Dario Kordic, yes. When he took the floor, he made a very extreme speech. Apart from the terrible statements made by Karadzic in the Assembly, I hadn't heard anything like it. He was referring to Zenica, the borders of Herceg-Bosna, about the oath they had taken, that they were going to defend Herceg-Bosna and Zenica, and I was amazed. So I walked out and I don't know what happened afterwards. However, I recall that the speech was very extreme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, the corps was now established. Did the role of the Municipal TO Staff change after that and what units did you have at your disposal after this?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, the Territorial Defence continued performing the tasks and duties pertaining to guarding facilities in Zenica. This was the Home Guard Unit, which was linked to its own territory on which it had been established. Of course new units were formed, and the idea arose that municipal and direct defence staffs had to be set up, but because we had to guard this large number of facilities which were targets not only for aggressor's forces but also for possible criminal gangs or sabotage units, we needed to retain a certain number of forces guarding these facilities. When the new organisation was set up, when the 3rd Corps was first established, the forces of the Municipal Defence Staff were reduced to three detachments which were -- which had men from the territories on which they were deployed. Zenica was divided into three sectors, and these three units were guarding facilities in these three sectors. Then there was the Municipal Staff that had three units for logistical support. This was now less than a thousand fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, among these important facilities, can you mention two or three that were truly significant not only for Zenica but for Bosnia and Herzegovina as a whole and as the Municipal Staff, was the guarding of these facilities your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was our main task at the time. For example, in the area whether the 1st Detachment was, there was the Vranduk tunnel which had to be guarded so that it would not be blocked up by anyone. In the area of the 2nd Detachment, there was the mine, the transformer stations. There was the Lasva junction, the junction in Blatusa and so on. And where the 3rd Detachment was, the main facility was the Klopce 2 transformer station. It was a large transformer station for the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina. There was another transformer station and a relay station in Klopce. And where the 2nd Detachment was, there was a radio relay station which had to be guarded. These were the major facilities. There were also bridges, school, banks, hospitals, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, where were the HVO units deployed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: In that period you mean? Well, in a way, we were -- well, I won't say we were deceived, but there was a story told by Zivko Totic, who was in fact doing something quite different. He asked us to get space in the KP Dom, the prison, and Kemal Kapetanovic had the meteorological institution and some other facilities. But at the same time he deployed his units, the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalion in dominant features around Zenica so as to observe movements. In other words, he wasn't carrying out the tasks that we had to perform, but he was saying that they were going to defend Zenica from any possible breakthrough by the enemy in the Vlasic area, so they started taking up positions at these elevations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at the last document in tab 12. Does this -- it's 1662. Does this reflect the deployment of the HVO forces that you have just been talking about? This is the last document in this set of documents. This document has no translation. It's 0786, the Jure Francetic Brigade. And tell me, what is this about and does this document reflect what you have just been saying?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as it is now time for a break, after the break I will ask the witness to indicate on the map the HVO positions in relation to Zenica which follow from this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will have our technical break now. This will allow the witness to rest for a while. It's quarter to 4.00, and we'll resume at about ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel may continue with their examination-in-chief now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the usher now show the witness a map, the scale of which is 1 to 50.000. It's a map of Zenica and it's in a set of maps called Zenica set 4/4/2. The scale of the map is 1 to 50.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, in the order, the number of which is 0786, could you please read out the zones of responsibility of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalion of the Jure Francetic Brigade and could you then mark the relevant positions on the map. Mark the map with the number "1" for the 1st Battalion and "2" for the 2nd Battalion, et cetera. This is in order to show the positions of the HVO units you were testifying about before the break.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the order of the command of the operative zone of Central Bosnia," such and such a number, dated the 20th of March, 1993. And in connection with the newly developed situation and the aggressor's attack on - and it's not very legible here - "We here issue the following Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond order: Order to -- reconnaissance, under number 1. Establish -- in the Catholic cemetery sector of the village of Raspotocje and monitor the movement of the ABiH army in the garrison. The labour organisation Grijanje and both the roads leading to the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please encircle the area and mark it with a Roman I so that we can be sure, so that we can know that it's the 1st Battalion that is in question.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion was deployed in this area, along this line, Raspotocje, Vucjak, then we have this elevation here. And they controlled this road that leads by the left bank of the Bosna River towards the Lasva. And as these are elevated features in relation to these roads, they controlled the road to the right of the River Bosna, on the right bank of the River Bosna. And this is where the barracks were located, and there was the unit of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of this line that you have just drawn to indicate the position of the 1st Battalion, could you draw a circle and mark it with Roman I.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion reached to the depth in Ovnak. This was its depth in Saracevica, Debela Medja, Zvecaj, Janjicki Vrh. That was the depth of the battalion. And this would more or less be its zone of responsibility, the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please have a look at the area in which the 2nd Battalion was deployed. Could you read out the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Number 2. The zone of responsibility of the 2nd Battalion. "Establish an observation post in the Negraj sector. I'll mark Negraj here. Above the village of Gradisce Jankovici, Jokivici, this is where the observation post was. "In order to observe the access towards Lisac." You can't see Lisac here, but you have the television and radio relay tower there. "Towards the village of Gradisce. This is the area called Gradisce. And Zmajevac, Zmajevac is a very important feature. Zmajevac is located here. The 2nd Battalion had its forces deployed in this area. There's a part that you can't see on the map. It goes towards Strnokosi and Gradisce; Zmajevac is here. Other parts of the forces were near the village of Stranjani. This is where the 2nd Battalion was. This was its zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the area where the 3rd Battalion was deployed in relation to the town of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The zone of responsibility of the 3rd Battalion, establish an observation post in the village of Kopilo sector. Kopilo is a village that is in this area to the right. So establish an observation post in the village of Kopilo sector in order to monitor the roads leading to the village of Arnauti, et cetera. This is the road here, from Zenica, Crkvica, Babino, Briznik, Arnauti, et cetera, these are the villages and the depth. "Control the road leading towards Perin Han. That's the road that continues here towards Lasva. The 3rd Battalion -- well, there's this area here near Crkvica too. The 3rd Battalion had the zone of responsibility on the right bank of the river of Bosna, and I could indicate this in this manner. Here is the Crkvica hill. So this would more or less be the area where the 3rd Battalion was located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reconnaissance platoon?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The reconnaissance platoon of the Jure Francetic Brigade should engage its forces to monitor the sector of Kuber and the road from Cajdras, Stranjani, Pojskent [phoen], and Ovnak. You can see that this was a mobile manoeuvre unit which was engaged in this area, from the top of Vjetrenice -- from the peak of Vjetrenice there's a road that passes through Saracevica and Kuber and then links up with Kacuni and continues in the direction of Busovaca municipality. This is the route it follows. So that would be the location of the reconnaissance platoon. And then there is this road towards Zenica and Vjetrenice and Cajdras. And the following road from -- crossroads at Cajdras leads towards Stranjani, Ovnak, et cetera. As you can see, this is the north-western part of Zenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we have now seen the positions of the HVO -- but I do apologise. To make things easier to follow, could you just mark the letters "IP" for reconnaissance patrol, and "C" for company on these roads?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the access here and here we have the reconnaissance patrol of the company. These are the three reconnaissance platoons that were engaged along these axes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as the important feature that is you controlled, you -- among the important features you controlled, you mentioned the Lasva junction. Towards the beginning of 1993, could you tell me whether there was any fighting which made that junction the focus of attention and did the Municipal TO Staff ask and receive assistance to carry out its task?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The Lasva junction is a very important feature in the territory of Zenica municipality, and according to peacetime plans it also had a very important role. Certain forces had been planned for this feature. If there was a crisis situation, if there was a war, these forces should provide direct security for it and also provide security for its depth, because this is a very important junction which connects Zenica to Travnik, Busovaca, and above all with the municipalities that are south of Zenica, Kakanj, Visoko, and further on Sarajevo. So this was an extremely important strategic feature. It was at the junction of roads. There were viaducts there. There were bridges over the Bosna and the Lasva, and it was important enough to protect. It was a very essential and expensive feature. So certain forces had always been planned to provide protection for it. However, at one time, when relations were quite calm, the -- part of the forces securing the feature weren't very strong. But as the tension increased, as the situation became more complex, part of the road in the vicinity of the junction towards Busovaca had been threatened by the HVO. We believed that it was necessary to provide more -- stronger forces to protect the junction, to prevent it from being destroyed or taken. If it had been -- if it had been taken or destroyed, it would have prevented -- it would have blocked the road between Zenica and Sarajevo. Since the situation was becoming increasingly complex at the time, increasingly tense, we didn't have a sufficient amount of forces to secure the junction. As a result we asked for assistance. We asked the 3rd Corps to provide us with reinforcements to make sure that the junction was adequately protected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive such reinforcements and which unit came to reinforce the forces guarding the junction?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally this didn't take place immediately. The 3rd Corps didn't have enough available forces for such action and they believed we had some forces on the battlefield in Maglaj. After a few exchanges, the 3rd Corps sent a unit from the 7th Brigade, a unit from the 7th, and later a unit from the 303rd, I think. They were sent as reinforcements to protect the junction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now, sir, look at the document in tab 11, that's document 456 [Realtime transcript read in error "4576"] of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you please read paragraph 2 and tell me whether this is the unit that was sent as a reinforcement for the Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Question 2: "The 7th Muslim Brigade with part of the forces continue defence and active combat operations against the Chetniks in the Bijelo Bucje area. Resubordinate the 1st Company, which is deployed in Zenica to the commander of the Zenica Municipal Staff, which will carry out tasks according to the decision of the staff commander."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just correct the transcript. The number of the document Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond is 406, and by mistake the transcript reads "4576." Thank you. Would you now please look at tab number 10, Prosecution Exhibit P310.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Have you found it? Do you recognise this document? Is it a document issued by your staff?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a document issued by the Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it confirms that this company became part of the Municipal Staff and was resubordinated to the Zenica Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the importance of this communication and the Lasva junction, would you please look at the document in tab 9, Prosecution Exhibit P210. This document has been issued by the 3rd Corps. To whom is it addressed, Mr. Ibrakovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: You can see from this that it was addressed to the Municipal Staff of the defence of Zenica and to the Kakanj Municipal Staff, and it's about securing a road. Under "2" it says: "The Zenica Municipal Staff shall use some of its forces to permanently secure and maintain the Zenica-Lasva, village of -- Dusina village of Sudine road for the needs of our armed forces, and the signature is that of Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, did you implement this order and did you understand what road you were supposed to secure?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In spite of the difficult and complex situation, we immediately implemented this order. Certain communications had been blocked up in the direction of Busovaca, and the only road from Zenica to Busovaca, the part of Busovaca where the army forces were, and the population that the HVO had not yet expelled, was this communication leading from Zenica through Lasva, the village of Dusina, the village of Sudine in the direction of Kacuni and this communication was very important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask the usher to give you another map and I would like you to draw this road on the map, the road that you had to secure. This is an excerpt from a map already admitted into evidence, Dusina 4/2. It's -- the scale is 25.000.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Look at the order and indicate on the map what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the junction in question. And along here the HVO had blocked up this road. This road leads towards Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca. And very close to the junction the road had already been damaged. The only communication leading to Lasva was along this road -- the village of Lasva, I mean, along the left bank of the River Bosna. That's the road. Up to the village of Lasva and the Lasva railway station. And then it went up through the hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lasva, Dusina, Sudine?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now from Dusina this road went towards Sudine. As far as I can tell probably it went along here. I don't see that it went here. It's possible that you could have taken an alternative route. I'm not absolutely sure now. It's one of these two. I'm marking them Roman I and Roman II, but I think Roman I is this road. I passed along this road, but now it's -- it's more or less the same. What is important is the section of road from the Lasva junction to the railway station in the village of Lasva and then up to Dusina. On route from Dusina the road was very bad, which is why the order mentions maintaining the communication. In winter, vehicles couldn't pass through certain sections. This was a temporary road for horse-drawn vehicles, so that you had to use tractors and horses to pull out vehicles that had become stuck there. So it was important to maintain this communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, where you circled "Lasva," would you mark that with "1," and could you mark the communication showing the direction from Lasva towards the village of Sudine.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the report you submitted to the 3rd Corps, Prosecution number 310, it says that this order was carried out and that units were put in a state of combat readiness. Tell me, as the Municipal Staff, did you ever issue an order for the use of these units in combat?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course not, and all our orders were quite to the contrary. To avoid any conflict, not to open fire unless in extreme need, if our forces were attacked. So not for a single moment was there ever such an order that fire should be opened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We shall tender these two documents later on. Would you please put the date on them and sign them and I will continue with my examination.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you did not issue an order for the use of the units in combat, tell me, was there a time when you started receiving information that there was fighting going on in this area, and what kind of information was this, if any?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that certain convoys were using this communication, it was being used in other words, the unit securing this communication of course worked in shifts. One shift would be eight hours long. One part of the unit would be there for eight hours. Then they would go to rest and be replaced by another part of the unit. And this functioned quite well. However, around the 26th and the 27th, we received information that there had been an incident up there, that there had been fighting, and that some sort of combat activities had taken place leading to the conflict we were trying to avoid. In any case, we received information to this effect, and I think it was in the afternoon on the 26th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any information about casualties?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, there was. I remember at that time - because I had some other duties to attend to - various kinds of information came. People would arrive from there in a state of panic, and they carried all sorts of information and one didn't really know what the actual situation was. And then we ordered the command of the 2nd Detachment to send people up there to see what was actually going on. In the evening hours, we received information that two members of the army had been killed, that there had also been losses on the HVO side - I don't know how many casualties - and the operations organ of the 2nd Detachment at Lapoce [phoen] sent this information. As for this other information, we didn't know how reliable it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your information, did some of it indicate that there may have been a murder up there or murders?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no reason to suspect that on that day. The only information we had was that there had been a conflict, that fire had been opened on both sides, and that there were casualties on both sides, that people on both sides had been killed. As for suspicions that a crime might have been committed, we only received some indications on the following day or a few days later that something like that might have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If such information arrived on the following day, tell me, as these units were under your command, was there an order that these suspicions should be investigated and did your Municipal Staff in some way participate in this, if there was any investigation? And if so, who?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been trying to concentrate on this period of time and recollect it. According to our chain of command from the District Staff, I think the commander of the District Staff at that time was Mr. Merdan and he asked that an investigation should be carried out to see if anything at all had happened up there, apart from the combat activity. This suspicion required that the commander do whatever fell within his competence. I remember that the commander got our security officer to look into it, and I think also our intelligence officer. The security officer was told to go, and there was also a team from the corps, to carry Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond out an on-site investigation and establish what had happened. In other words, the commander sent his assistance for security to investigate the suspicion. He later returned and reported to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Ibrakovic: Do you know who in Zenica conducted this investigation? Was the court informed and do you know whether there was in fact an investigation and what were its results?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
