utterances.text: When our security assistant returned, he informed the commander that a team had been up there, an extended team, including the military prosecutor and the court investigator as well as members of a department of the security services centre that was an expert team, and there was also someone from the civilian protection and organs of the civil police. And from his report to the commander, I concluded that certain measures had been taken and that the most competent people had gone up there to establish what had happened. Apparently the HVO had intervened. They were prone to exaggerate things and they said that a crime had been committed. So this entire team went up there to investigate and establish what had actually happened. And we all understood that everything possible had been done at that point in time. Now with hindsight, I think that really everything that was possible and that could have been done at that moment was done in order to investigate the situation, and it was established that no crime had been committed in the Lasva local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were the Chief of Staff, the security organ was not part of the staff. It was linked to the commander. Is that what you've just been saying? Because he reported to the commander, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. The security officer was an assistant to the commander. I was the Chief of Staff, and I did not have the competency or any kind of power over the security organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although this might sound like a leading question, but tell me, you personally did not go to conduct any on-site investigation. It was the competent organs whose job it was. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to belabour this point, so would you now just tell me, please: Apart from this company that was resubordinated to you and part of the fighters from the PDO who were not at the Maglaj war theatre, were there any other large units of the BH army up there?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: With your permission, I would like to say something about the HVO forces in Lasva at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to go into that now. I am only asking you to tell me how many fighters of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in your opinion were active in that area at that point in time. I'm referring to parts of the PDO and the 7th Muslim Company that had been resubordinated to you. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that we had a reinforced platoon up there, about 20 to 30 combatants. They were providing security for all those features in that area. Naturally, most of the men at that time -- most of the men of the TO and the PDO, were on the Maglaj battlefield, because every 15 days we would send a company to Maglaj to hold certain lines. We had a line that was being held there to prevent the Chetniks from penetrating. At that time, there was a unit from that PDO there because the schedule had been made in time and we knew which unit would be going there in 15 days' time, et cetera. So that unit was down there, and that area wasn't as well defended then. And the company that came from the 7th, that had about 60 men - I don't know whether it had more than that, because at the time the companies were never up to full strength. Some men were on leave. Some were on sick leave. So I don't believe there were more than 80 to 100 combatants in that area at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the document that's been admitted into evidence, in the HVO document it says that there were eight and a half thousand men from the ABiH up there. What would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well -- well, if we had had so many men, we would have been in Sarajevo. I apologise, Your Honours. This was just a joke, but the HVO at that time was spreading incredible propaganda and saying that there were camps and massacres and murders in Zenica. It said that there were various substantial forces there. So the propaganda was worthy of a Goebbels so I'm not at all surprised by some information. As I said, I mentioned 80 do 100 men, so you can see the difference of opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ibrakovic, we've mentioned Mr. Zivko Totic, the commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade. We've mentioned him on a number of occasions. Did you at any point in time find that Zivko Totic had been kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The entire town was aware of that on the 15th of April, 1993. I think that's the date there was an incident in the territory of the Pobrijezje local commune. Zivko Totic was kidnapped on that occasion, and we found out about that, I think, around noon. I can't be precise, but it was around noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an order of any kind from the 3rd Corps Command -- or, rather, did your commander order you to do anything in relation to this affair?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally this was an exceptional situation, an incident that caught us all by surprise. And in the afternoon, the commander called me to his office and he said that I should report to the 3rd Corps Command. He said I should report to the commander, Enver Hadzihasanovic, in order to be assigned a certain task that concerned the affair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what sort of task were you assigned, if you were assigned a task, and was the task carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally I said that the commander was quite agitated, he was angry that the problem had arisen in a certain sense. He gave us a task orally. He said that all measures should be taken to locate Mr. Zivko Totic. Naturally, since I was familiar with the territory - I was born in Zenica - and since the task he issued was issued to me orally, the commander told me that I, together with a certain group that was already ready, and together with part of military security and part of the military police and together with the civilian police, members of the MUP with vehicles and together with a certain number of policemen, I was told to go to the axis of Zenica, Crkvica, Babino, and as far as the final village the last village in that area. Once this task had been assigned to me, we left. I left with this team in three or four vehicles and with the necessary escort. We headed off in that direction. We tried to identify certain traces, to interview certain people. We reached the last village, which was the village of Arnauti, and we also spoke to some members of the unit who were present there and to the inhabitants. We went to buildings where we thought that Zivko Totic might be detained, if he was in the area. Naturally, we did not succeed in finding any traces. We then returned to the corps command, the command of the 3rd Corps, and told the commander that we hadn't found Zivko Totic in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me: Which part of your PDO, anti-sabotage detachment, was in the village of Arnauti when you went there and spoke to them?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the village of Arnauti is one of the remotest villages in the municipality of Zenica and it's on the border with the municipality of Kakanj. It's quite elevated. It's located in a forest. And part of the forces were there. They were part of the 3rd PDO. We had a unit up there the strength of one platoon, and they were providing security for certain features in that area, because the territory of the municipality of Zavidovici has a few axes that could be used by the Serbian and Chetnik forces to approach Zenica from that direction. So they were controlling that territory and the features that led towards the territory where the Serbs were present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently discover who had in fact kidnapped Mr. Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Mr. Saric and I were on good terms and we were on good terms with Mr. Zivko Totic. We were friendly. Apart from our military duties, we would often speak to each other, not just for military purposes, and I felt a little sorry for the man. So we were interested in the case, and two or three days later we found out that the Arabs were responsible for the kidnapping. But this was not part of our responsibilities. We couldn't deal with the matter any more. This is the information we received, and then we stopped thinking about the -- the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Ibrakovic, tell me whether you in some way participated in the fighting that took place at the beginning of June 1993 in the territory of your municipality too.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1992 and in the brief clashes at the beginning of 1993, the territory in the municipality of Zenica was quite open. There were no lines and there was no possibility for fighting, for combat action. But when the conflict with the HVO started, part of the territory, towards Travnik and Vitez, Narovnak [phoen], was under the control of HVO forces. And in the immediate vicinity, below that feature, there were a few villages, a few Zenica villages inhabited by Bosniaks. And in a certain sense they were irritated and provoked from the HVO lines. Very frequently there were requests to have this line moved beyond the pass so that they wouldn't threaten them, because they couldn't work on the land. Snipers provoked them, and they were provoked in a few other ways. There were quite a few wounded men, quite a few wounded people, and pressure was exerted on the staff to ensure that the line was moved beyond the pass. But we didn't have enough forces. We didn't have forces that were ready to do something of that kind. Because these were individuals who could only defend certain features and territory that hadn't been occupied by the aggressor. These were home guards of a sort. So there was this problem. And it was also a problem because we had contact with neighbours of ours. It was also our duty to exchange information with these neighbours. And I remember that there was a very difficult situation in the Travnik municipality, especially in the part of the municipality in the Bila Valley. And the traditional ties between these villages on one side of the Ovnak and on the other side of the Ovnak - they were Bosniak villages then - well, the inhabitants found that their lives had become extremely complicated. In that time, the HVO was acting in a very aggressive way in the area beyond the hill. They were acting aggressively towards the Bosniaks and other people. They would move them out of their houses, expel them. So they were acting very aggressively. But we did not do anything, nor could we do anything. We didn't have the forces. But on the whole, the situation was becoming increasingly complex.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what happened at the beginning of June? Were you assigned a specific task? If so, what sort of task were you assigned and what happened subsequently?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the beginning of June - I think it was on the 4th or 5th. It's probably the 5th - I was contacted through my commander, because the commander would often go to see Mr. Hadzihasanovic to be briefed by him. And in the evening hours, my commander said, "You have to report this evening to the 7th Brigade command and you are to assist the 7th Brigade officers in drafting certain documents." The men had insufficient experience and training and they weren't capable of drafting certain documents, so I went to the 7th command. I was assigned a certain task by the commander of the 7th, Mr. Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that you drafted the documents in question. And at any point in time, did the units from Zenica set off to assist the units in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I was informed of the fact that a tactical group had been established that was supposed to carry out a certain plan which involved linking up the forces in Zenica with the forces in the Bila Valley. As far as I know, the forces there at the time were in a very difficult position, so they were supposed to be assisted. The forces were supposed to be linked up. Naturally, in the course of the night and on the basis of Mr. Kubura's main idea, I and Mr. Kubura's assistants drafted orders, issued orders for the units that had been designated as units that would participate in the action, and naturally maps were also drawn. Everything was done that should be done for an organised unit. We carried out that task overnight and the task had been completed by the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you start carrying out the task and what sort of resistance did you encounter from the HVO in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's easy to prepare such things on paper, but in reality things are a little different and a little more difficult. The main and initial position was taken up by the units during the night between the 6th and 7th, naturally, on the base of the document s that we had drafted the previous evening. The action was to commence in the early morning hours, and naturally it did commence, but we encountered fierce resistance, extremely fierce resistance. Naturally, it's impossible to conceal anything, and the information had leaked somehow. The HVO on the Ovnak line, which is the dominant line, well, this line had been fortified in a way that we hadn't expected. The line had been very well prepared and covered. So on that day, we didn't manage to do much. We had to halt the action. We had to amend the order in a certain sense. We had to regroup the forces. And on the following day, at the same time, we wanted to make another attempt at opening up the road towards Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, now that so many years have passed, do you know anything about how intense the fighting was when Novo Selo was liberated at the top of Ovnak and when other dominant elevations on that day were liberated?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: According to the new amended order, the attack was launched very early in the morning. HVO units that had probably brought in reinforcements during the day and night opened very intense fire, and the pace of the attack did not go ahead as planned. At around eleven o'clock, we managed to break through to the line above Novo Selo. That's on the attack axis for the main forces. The auxiliary forces remained at the initial positions. The task of these forces was to take the Strmac feature that dominated the valley. Naturally, they didn't succeed in doing much; although, well, two or three units were focussed there and there were certain misunderstandings. About 2.00 or 3.00 in the afternoon, we succeeded in breaking through to the line near Novo Selo and Cukle. That was the immediate task. And I know that it was not until 2000 hours that the HVO flag on Strmac was taken down. It was only around 2000 hours on the 8th that that action came to an end. So things proceeded quite slowly. It was quite difficult. There was fierce fighting for specific features, and it wasn't until 2000 hours that Strmac was taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ibrakovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does the other Defence team have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We only have a few questions for today's witness on behalf of Mr. Kubura. As the witness talked about this operation in early June, I ask that Prosecution Exhibit P420 be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P420, Mr. Registrar. Cross-examined by Mr. Ibrisimovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrakovic, you took part in drawing up the documentation, that is, the orders in respect of these military activities in early June, so I'm asking you, is this document familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the command of the tactical group, and it's an attack order. Please look at paragraph 2 of the document. The tactical -- the -- the tactical group is composed of units of the 7th Brigade, a detachment of the 314th Motorised Brigade, a company of the Manevar Detachment, a PDO company, and a unit from the 314th Brigade; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now please look at page 2. In paragraph 5.1, in this operation the 2nd and 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade will participate?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the same paragraph, the axis of attack of the 7th Muslim Brigade is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at paragraph 5.3.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which indicates that the Manevar Detachment, the Ministry of the Interior cooperating with a detachment from the 314th Brigade is to take control of Strmac and, as the next task, take control of Grahovcici. I assume it's the village of Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this what the order for attack says?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at paragraph 5.4, please, which indicates that a detachment from the 314th Brigade jointly with the Manevar Detachment is to take control of the village Grahovcici-Vrpce line.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in paragraph 5.3 and paragraph 5.4 in this attack order one can see that the 7th Muslim Brigade did not go in the direction of the village of Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were all my questions. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I would like to have the document back, but in B/C/S. And I'll have a question to put to the witness a little later. The Prosecution may take the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Daryl Mundis, and along with my colleagues here today, we represent the Prosecution in this case. As the Presiding Judge told you earlier this afternoon, we will have some questions for you; although, we certainly won't take as much time as my learned colleagues from the Defence did. At the outset, sir, let me simply indicate to you that it's not our intention in any way to confuse you. And in the event you find any of my questions confusing, if you simply tell me that, I will rephrase the question so that you understand what it is I'm asking you. Let me start out, sir, by asking you a few questions about the events in the Lasva local commune or the village of Dusina towards the end of January 1993. You -- you answered some questions about that. I have just a few additional questions for you. You told us, I believe, that at the time of the events in Dusina, late January 1993, that Dzemal Merdan was the district staff commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, until approximately when Dzemal Merdan was the district staff commander? When did he cease being the district staff commander?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It's like this, for the sake of clarification: As the 3rd Corps was established, certain elements and services and commanding officers were designated from the command of the district staff and transferred to positions in the 3rd Corps. That's what the order provided for. The core of the 3rd Corps was formed from the District Staff. Part of the officers from the District Staff were transferred to the 3rd Corps. This process took place over a certain period of time. One officer after another was transferred from the District Staff to the 3rd Corps according to certain plans which I'm not familiar with. The District Staff was slowly disbanded over a period of two to three months. That's why I can't be sure of the exact time. Some officers may have even held two posts simultaneously. This process went on over some time, so I cannot be precise in my answer, but I think that it was in April or March -- at any rate, in the spring that this staff was disbanded, and I don't think that Dzemal Merdan was the last officer in that staff. However, this transformation took place over a period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just told us that you believed that some officers may have held two posts simultaneously. And I suggest to you that in fact Dzemal Merdan was one such person, because in late January 1993 he was also the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I didn't think about that. I didn't look into it. It wasn't within my competence. So I don't know what you want me to say. In any rate -- at any rate, I saw Dzemal Merdan as superior to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was because as part of the Zenica Municipal Staff you reported to the District Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the District Staff was operating, we received and implemented tasks according to the orders and decisions of the District Staff, among others, because this was a period of transformation, when Municipal Staffs and District Staffs were being disbanded. This, you have to understand, was a transitional period. You couldn't simply do it overnight because certain activities had to be carried on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, turning again or turning more specifically to the events in Dusina in late January 1993. You told us about a team that went to Dusina in order to investigate what had occurred there. Is that -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, from what I -- from what I knew, I received this information from our security officer, and this team went there to establish the true state of affairs and to see whether there were grounds to suspect that something had happened in the village of Dusina beyond normal combat activities. This was a highly expert team, the best that could be assembled at that time in Zenica municipality, very professional people. Because the army was still in the process of being established -- I mean the 3rd Corps, and it didn't yet have all the necessary organs or equipment. This is a very expert job. As you know, you need professionals to do it. It can't be done by volunteers or lay people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I understand what you told us earlier, this team included, among other, someone from the security services centre, a military prosecutor, a court investigator, someone from civilian protection, and someone from the civilian police. At least that's what's recorded in the English transcript. Do you recall the names of any of these people?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us the names of the people that you remember who formed part of this team and which position those persons had.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that Vlado Adamovic went there. He was, I think, the military prosecutor. I can't be absolutely sure, but he was employed in the military prosecutor's office. Then I know that Mr. Mesic went there on behalf of the civilian protection. I can't remember the names of the people from the security services centre. They were forensic technicians and policemen, authorised personnel. But according to the report by the assistant commander for security, they were part of the team, and I don't know which of the court investigators went there. I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "the report by the assistant commander for security," do you remember who that person was at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, the assistant commander for security in the Municipal Staff was Zulfikar Bojcic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this report that Mr. Karbojcic [sic] produced, did you read that report, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't a written report. It was just oral information to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to whom did Mr. Karbojcic present this oral report?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: To the commander

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name of the commander at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jasmin Saric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember -- let me ask you this: Were you present when this oral report was given to the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't present when he was briefing the commander, but just after he had seen the commander he came to my office and we exchanged information orally. As far as I know, there was no written report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if when you received this briefing from Mr. Karbojcic whether he informed you as to the steps that were taken, in terms of trying to find out exactly what happened in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question because there are no grounds for it in the witness's reply. The witness said that this gentleman only briefed the commander and that afterwards he exchanged a few pieces of information with him. So the question cannot be put in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you exchanged information orally with Mr. Karbojcic, did you obtain any information from him concerning the methodology used by this team to determine what happened in Dusina in late January 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the information I received, I gained the impression that everything had been done. We didn't go into details, but I understood that everything that had to be done had been done, so I didn't really deal with this matter any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Karbojcic tell you or did you ask him whether any people had been interviewed in the village of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I repeat, it didn't fall within my competence and I didn't want to interfere in this activity because it was being done by another organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I -- if I understand you correctly, sir - and tell me if I'm mistaken - Mr. Karbojcic informed you that the team had concluded that there were no crimes committed in Dusina but didn't go into detail in terms of informing you how that conclusion was reached.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Karbojcic didn't say that, because he himself was not expert enough to say such things. I only learned these things later on. But he did say that an expert team had been present up there on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I -- I'm a bit confused, sir. What exactly did he tell you this expert team did?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: That they were up there, on the ground. Because someone who doesn't know what has to be done is not expert enough, cannot enter into the essence of the problem. He simply established that these people were up there and then he withdrew and brought this information back to us. I don't know what is not clear here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question then goes to -- to the point: Did he inform you that the conclusion was no crimes were committed, or did he simply tell you that this team went to Dusina?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The latter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you subsequently found out from other sources that no crime had been committed in Dusina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: After the expert team had done part of their job, that's when this conclusion was reached. It couldn't be reached right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall from whom it was that you learned or were told that no crimes had been committed in Dusina?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the setting or the context in which you were informed of that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer to this question, but most probably during conversations, at meetings. But it wasn't official. It was nothing official. It was during informal conversations and meetings that I gained this information. Because nobody was duty-bound to brief the Municipal Staff about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. It might be a good point in time for the next technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's half past 5.00 now. We'll have our technical break, and we'll resume at about five to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn now to the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, which you told us about or testified about earlier this afternoon. You told us, if I recall correctly, that you found out about the kidnapping on the day it happened, that is, the 15th of April, 1993, about noon. Do you recall how you found out about this or who told you about this event?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't remember who told me about the event, but the entire town knew about it, so the information may have been forwarded from a number of sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you were ordered to report to the 3rd Corps commander in order to be assigned a task in relation to this event and that when you got there, the 3rd Corps commander was angry. I'm wondering if Commander Hadzihasanovic said anything to you or explained anything to you about why he was angry about this event.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't. I had the impression that he had been quite affected by the event, but he didn't say anything in particular about it, as far as I can remember right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us, sir, that you went to the remote village of Arnauti pursuant to the tasking that you received. Can you tell us why you were sent to Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was sent to the Zenica-Crkvice-Babino-Briznik-Arnauti axis. That is the area -- that's the part of the territory of the municipality of Zenica that was concerned. And Arnauti is the last village in that area and it borders with the municipality of Kakanj. There were no other villages beyond that point, there was just a forest there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say, sir, there were no villages beyond Arnauti, just the forest, at that point in time, in the spring of 1993, was there a road from Arnauti to Kakanj through the forest?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was some sort of an alternative forest road that could be used during certain periods of the year, but it was in a pretty poor condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, who you spoke to when you reached the village of Arnauti and who -- or the subject of the discussion as it related to the kidnapping of Commander Totic.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I arrived in the village of Arnauti, I spoke to a number of local people there. There were also members of TO units. There were representatives of the local commune. There were the local inhabitants, and so on. So I spoke to a number of individuals, but I really can't remember their names. There were a number of individuals I spoke to, but I wouldn't single out any of the individuals. There weren't any important names. I can't even remember the commander of the unit. I can't remember his name and I can't remember what he looked like either. There were a lot of people there, a lot of contacts, and quite a lot of time has passed since then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was there one TO unit in Arnauti at that time or more than one TO unit in Arnauti in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: There was just one TO unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was one of the anti-sabotage detachments?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was part of that unit, because that detachment covered the entire right bank of the Bosna River, from Perin Han to Klopce, Crkvica. That was a fairly wide area. Because the territory was divided into three sectors and there was PDO that covered that territory. Part of the unit that only secured some features up there was located in that narrowest stretch of territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the TO unit or part of a TO unit that was in Arnauti, were there any other units of the ABiH in Arnauti in the middle of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. And it wasn't necessary for any other unit to be present in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us earlier this afternoon that Arabs were responsible for the kidnapping of Zivko Totic, and I'm wondering how you came across that information.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether I received that information from Vinko Baresic, who at the time was Zivko Totic's deputy. Perhaps it was from someone else, but that's the information I received at the time, and I couldn't really say who I received it from. I spoke to Vinko about the subject, but I don't know whether I received the information from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, when approximately did you speak to Commander Totic's deputy, Vinko Baresic concerning this kidnapping? Was it sometime in the spring of 1993, or was it several years after the war? When approximately was it you spoke to him about this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: At the time. Vinko and I knew each other from before, and we discussed things. It was during that period. I can't remember the exact date, but it was during that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember receiving any information after the kidnapping from any ABiH or 3rd Corps or TO officials concerning the kidnapping? Was it discussed at any TO Staff meetings or at any meetings that you were aware of of any units of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, because I never attended those meetings. The commander was the one who attended them, so I really don't remember. But I at least did not receive such information at such meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware or did you ever become aware of where Commander Totic was held during the time he had been kidnapped?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, never. I never became aware of that, and I never concerned myself with that issue. I had other problems to deal with that were far more important. It was only after the war that I saw Zivko and obtained some kind of information. But I don't really like talking about -- I don't really enjoy talking about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware in the spring of 1993 that there were persons that you've described as Arabs in Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's true. When I arrived in Arnauti, I saw some people there, but I didn't think that they were members of any particular units, but they were reminiscent of members of such units [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you mean, sir, when you say "they were reminiscent of members of such units." What do you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. In fact, I said they did not make me think that they were members of such units because --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The translation in 67.5 is quite wrong. I've just noticed that. It say that is they were reminiscent of members of certain units. The witness quite clearly stated that they did not resemble members of certain units, which is quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I thank my colleague for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: What were those people that you saw in Arnauti wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: What were they wearing? Well, they were wearing sort of clothes the people wore at the time. People wore whatever they had. They were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Did you see any persons who appeared to be of Middle Eastern or North African origin in Arnauti in mid-April 1993 when you went there to try to find out what had happened to Zivko Totic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I have said, there was only the unit -- the Territorial Defence unit that was present there. There were some people who looked as if they were something like that. They looked as if they were Arabs. Because at the time in Zenica there was a number of humanitarian organisations, and that is the link I made. I made such a link. There were organisations present that were helping the people, and they were acting in a humanitarian capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these Arabs or persons that you say appeared as though they might have been Arabs, what type of clothing were they wearing in Arnauti in mid-April 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, they were wearing civilian clothes, shirts of some kind, waistcoats worn by civilians. They had beards, and that's what made them resemble the people you have been mentioning, but otherwise they were in no way different from the inhabitants of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, whether these persons were armed or unarmed.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: They weren't armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, that they were otherwise in no way different from the inhabitants of the village, can you tell us whether or not it appeared to you that their skin colour was such that they were from Middle Eastern or North African countries?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they left the impression -- or I was under the impression that they were such people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of these people on the day you were in Arnauti searching for information about Mr. Totic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any information or any knowledge about -- let me strike that question. How, to the best of your recollection, was the Zivko Totic kidnapping incident resolved? How did it come to a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The incident itself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, the resolution. Did Mr. Totic eventually -- was he released? How did that -- to the best of your recollection, what happened? How did it resolve itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, since we received such information -- we received information according to which Arabs were involved in this, it was no longer a matter of interest and I found out, like all the other citizens in Zenica, that some sort of an exchange had taken place involving the Arabs. It took place two or three months after the incident. I don't know how long afterwards this thing happened exactly, but I know that there was an exchange and the European Mission acted as an intermediary, which that's the right name of the organisation that was involved in the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, other than the Arabs that were involved in this kidnapping, did you ever receive any information from any source indicating that there may have been Bosnians or Bosniaks involved in the kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never received any information of that kind, official or unofficial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn now to the last subject I'd like to cover with you. During the time period when -- in 1992, when the TO had a large number of units that were assigned to it, you told us at one point there were 127 different units including a TV unit. Is that -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No. The TV company had a group, and that group had one pistol, and the group was providing security for their studio to ensure that nothing was stolen from them. So that is the group that was protecting the entrance to the building and the building itself. So it was a security service. They were providing security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you told us - and this was on page 29, line 1 of today's transcript, the English transcript - that there were 127 different units, and earlier you had said that in addition to the Patriotic League there were many other formations that had come from other areas. Do you recall telling us that earlier this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in the Zenica area in 1992 whether there were any units that went by the name of Muslimanske Snage or MOS?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: There were no such forces in Zenica, but, you know, we're not soldiers in the full sense of the term, so certain terms that aren't military terms are accepted. So some of the inhabitants started using terms like MOS, HOS, and HVO. But such forces didn't officially exist, but this was the slang used by combatants and it gained currency. But as far as I know, there were no such formations. There were units that were part of the TO. They had their title. For example, the Lasva TO, Orahovica, or the Lasta TO detachment, the Stijena TO detachment. But the term "Muslim" wasn't used as part of the name. This was a term that was added by individuals, but such forces did not officially exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will now ask Defence counsel whether they have any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrakovic, in response so a question put to you by my learned colleague, you said that the regional staff was your immediate superior command in 1992 and you said that Mr. Dzemal Merdan was the commander of the Regional Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the chief of the staff was?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning, Vinko Baresic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, was Ramiz Dugalic in that position for a certain period of time? I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Ramiz Dugalic?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I do know Ramiz Dugalic personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although, you said that you were not in fact a real soldier, you nevertheless do know that -- or rather, you're nevertheless familiar with military terminology and you are familiar with military orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could P245 please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order from the Supreme Command Staff dated the 18th of November, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under A2, do you see the name of the individual listed there and do you see the position he was appointed to?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Under number two, there's the name of Merdan, Dzemal, deputy commander of the corps. That's the position he was appointed to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at item two on the second page at the top.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "The officers designated as acting officers in this order shall be relieved of the duties they had to date. "

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As someone who's in the Territorial Defence and later in the army units, does this mean that Mr. Dzemal Merdan after the 18th of November, 1992 was able to retain his previous position as commander of the Regional Staff or was he relieved of these duties?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: According to this document, no. But this period lasted for a certain time. So I don't know when this took place exactly. I don't know the exact date. But I can see that he was not the commander of the Regional Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document P200.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document from the Zenica District Defence Staff dated the 26th of January, 1993. Have a look at the signature on the second page, please. Can you tell me whose signature this is?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Ramiz Dugalic. It's Ramiz Dugalic's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the commander assumes other duties, what sort of position does the Chief of Staff have?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: He change it is -- or he replaces the commander in his absence and someone else performs those duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In relation to a question put to you by my learned colleague about Mr. Bojcic, if I have understood you correctly, you said that you didn't have detailed information about the matter and you didn't go to the site yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have personal information about the way in which the investigation was carried out, or was it secondhand information?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The knowledge you had about the investigation, was this direct knowledge that you had? Were you present at the site? Or did you find out about the location of the investigation from others?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go to the scene myself. It was only after about two months that I went to that area. And the information I obtained was obtained from others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever examine documents drafted by the Security Services Centre or been an investigating judge or is this also information that you obtained from others?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any such documents because I wasn't responsible for this and none had the duty of informing the Municipal Staff or the chief of the Municipal Staff. In particular, I never saw those documents during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ibrakovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have a few questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you left the Municipal Staff, you said that you assumed the duties of commander. According to the transcript, it says the 330th Brigade was concerned. You became the commander of which unit exactly? Could you please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the 330th Light Brigade, which was part of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the 330th Light Brigade, which town was it located in? Where were its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, when the transformation, when the change took place, it was no longer necessary for the staffs to continue to exist, from the first anti-sabotage detachment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was precise: Where was your command office, your office -- your command office for the 330th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: My command, my office was in Bistricak, which is about 30 kilometres to the north of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Was the 330th Light Brigade attached to an operational group? We have heard testimony according to p according to which there were OG's in Bosnia. There was the Bosnia OG, the Lasva OG. There was the Bosanska Krajina OG. There was the Zapad or West OG. Was your light brigade attached to an OG?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was attached to the operative group 3 North.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, OG 3 North. Usher, could we place the map that we have referred to on the ELMO. It's the first map. You've indicated the position of the battalions of the HVO. You've marked the positions of three battalions. Are these positions valid for the entire year of 1993, or did they change in the course of that year?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The positions of the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Battalion were in the first half of 1993, until April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the map that you have used to indicate these positions corresponds to a situation that was valid up until the month of April. Because that wasn't said and it is important. So after April, this changed. The positions of the battalions changed after that date.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It changed. Very well. As we have the map before us, why not have a good look at it. Please use the pointer, because I don't think this has been done yet. Please use the pointer to indicate the location of the 3rd Corps headquarters -- we have a very large map before us, so could you use the map to indicate the position, the exact position, of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we can see the precise location. The Zenica Municipal Staff, where was this body located?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask you something about the kidnapping of Mr. Totic. You know that Mr. Totic was involved in an exchange and he was released. Do you remember his release, which must have been given extensive coverage in Zenica. Do you remember the day of his release? Can you recall the time when he was freed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that day because of the heavy presence of UN forces. There were white APCs and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you use the pointer to indicate the location at which Mr. Totic was released. Because you have just told us that this left a firm impression on your memory.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And when he was released, where was he released?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: At the stadium, this red building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because we have seen a video and we could see the stadium in the background. On that day, where were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I truly don't remember. I was in town. Because the Municipal Staff was in town. But I can't remember precisely where I was. You couldn't come close. There was a blockade around the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you said there were blockades. Who had erected these blockades, these barriers, you just said that it was blocked.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw white armoured personnel carriers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] White personnel carriers. Who did these white personnel carriers belong to? Which army? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The United Nations and their observers, as we called them. I don't know what their precise title was, but you know who I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the UN were responsible for these blockades, for these barriers?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't exactly a barrier, but the approach to that area was made impossible. Probably so that the exchange could take place more easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I would like P420 to be shown to you. Again, the B/C/S version, I kept it with me because I said I was going to use it later. Could you please place the document on the ELMO. So we have the first page there. And in response to a question put to you by Defence counsel, you said that you had assisted in drafting orders in the 7th Brigade. My question is: Did you contribute to drafting this document which consists of a number of pages and deals with a number of issues? Were you, intellectually speaking, involved in the drafting of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that one of the units from the Municipal Staff participated in this task - and that's the company from the PDO; it was a weakened company - on a certain axis I, as a representative of the Municipal Staff, participated in this tactical group. Therefore, I was appointed to the tactical group, as was the person from the 314th and so on. And of course I participated in drawing up this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you participated in drafting this document. When this order was typed out, you and others had already drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. In the process of work of a command, more than one person takes part. This document was typed out by some of the officers from the operations and training organ or, rather, their typists based on an outline that we gave them, and then they brought it to the commander for his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the commander signed it, and did you yourself read the order?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. Have a look at paragraph 5.1, item 5.1. 5.1 consists of two paragraphs. I would like you to read out the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "The second echelon will be made up of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Motorised Brigade, the 7th Muslim Brigade on the main axis of attack -- on the main axis of attack. The immediate task is to take control of -- the word" -- the line is missing -- "of the village of Cukle, Novo Selo, and the next task is to take control of the villages Brajkovici, Plavcici. The right-hand neighbour is the company of the second PDO OGO Zenica. The attack is supported by the PVG 2, the village of Vrselje and the next is Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the paragraph that I wanted you to read out. Have a look at paragraph 5.1. Have a look at the beginning of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second paragraph that begins with the words "Napad" in your language. It's line number 4. The word it starts with is "Napad," attack. Could you please read it out.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I didn't realise that this was the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please read it out.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "The attack will be carried out by three detachments. The first echelon will consist of the 2nd Detachment of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade with GG." I can't remember what "GG" stands for. "GD Planina on the first axis and the 2nd Detachment of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade on the auxiliary axis."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So my question in fact concerns the part that refers to GG Planina. According to the English translation that I have, the 2nd Detachment of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade together with Planina, or mountain, GG, and then it says Guca Gora. In military terms, what does "Planina" mean? What does "Planina" mean in military terms?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: It's probably one of the groups. Because you can see here that it wasn't battalions that were attacking. A battalion is lower than a brigade. Within the battalions, temporary groups were formed for this activity. Detachments, detachment -- a detachment does not exist in terms of establishment. There is a brigade, and the next lowest unit is a battalion, and then comes a company and then comes a platoon. There are no detachments. But for this activity probably smaller groups participated. A detachment is therefore part of a battalion. And "GG" can mean -- it can refer to some group, a name -- the "Planina," which means "mountain"," because when you're using means of communication and secret signals, instead of a name like "Mirso," for example, you use a number, in case the line is being intercepted. So "Planina," which means mountains, is probably the name of a group. Guca Gora is far away from us, so it can't be that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that "Planina" is the name of a group, but there's nothing else you can say. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm convinced that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any semantic issues you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I just wanted to say that Guca Gora was something added by the interpreters with a question mark. It's not something contained in the document itself, but it's something suggested by the translation service. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We should take note of the fact that Guca Gora in the English translation is perhaps an interpretation of the letters "GG," but the witness had another explanation. What would you say about the meaning of the letters "GG"?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: "GG" might refer to "group." Various names were given. It could be a -- an upper group, a group for chasing. I don't know. There are various possibilities. And after all this time, I really can't recall. But I'm convinced it refers to a group, because there were various groups being used at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for having provided that answer. The other Judges have no questions for you. Mr. Mundis, do you have any additional questions that relate to the questions that I have just put?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has just a few questions that relate to questions that Your Honour has put to the witness. Further cross-examination by Mr. Mundis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you that the initial "GG" in the document we were just looking at refer to "guerilla group."

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what you say. I would not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you familiar with a guerilla group that was named Planina Suma, or did you ever hear of a guerilla group Planina Suma?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I've never heard of it. I'm hearing about it for the first time now, from you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us the approximate date that you became the commander of the 330th Light Brigade with headquarters in the area of Bistricak.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recall that because it was a significant day in my life; the 24th of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, if you were aware or if you had any knowledge about training of guerilla groups in the area of Bistricak in the spring or late -- let me put it this way, in February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is not connected with the questions put by Your Honour or with the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Mundis, that has nothing to do with the questions I put to him. I didn't ask him if there were any guerilla groups in Bistricak. Why do you want to ask the witness this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Prosecution Exhibit P724 makes a reference to guerilla group Planina Suma being trained in the area of Bistricak in February 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't up there at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he wasn't there, because he assumed his duties in December, on the 24th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With all due respect, Mr. President, the question was simply whether he was aware of that going on in February 1993. It was simply whether he had any awareness or any knowledge of, in light of his position within the Zenica Municipal Staff, about training of a guerilla group with the name Planina Suma, as reflected in Prosecution Exhibit 724. That's simply the extent of the question and as far as we would be prepared to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have already answered the question, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I've heard this, now, from the prosecutor, this term Suma Planina or whatever it is. The first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution would like to know whether in February 1993 in Zenica, when you were the Chief of Staff, did you at that point in time hear about any guerilla groups or a guerilla group in Bistricak.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, if the witness still has the binder prepared by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look, sir, at the last document, that is, 786. My only question, sir, is: This map, which -- the map which you earlier drew the locations of the HVO unit around Zenica, His Honour the Presiding Judge asked you about the time period in which these units were in the locations as depicted on the map. And my question, sir, is whether or not the document numbered "786" was the basis for you making the markings on the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, as I told you previously, the HVO was playing a double role in Zenica. It was talking to us nicely, while at the same time they were taking up certain positions. Of course, we had information about this from the ground. We knew what they were doing, and we knew the approximate location of their commands in this location, as I indicated on the map. But this document is something I saw here. And on the basis of this document, I marked the position approximately. It's not entirely precise, but it's thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, it's -- it's difficult to tell from the photocopy, at least the one that we have, but I'm wondering if the copy that you have, the date of that document is legible.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Time, 12.00. Date, it seems to me to be dated in March 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no questions, but for the sake of the record, my learned friend mentioned document 5724, but it mentions neither guerillas nor Planina nor Suma, simply for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the other Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would ask that this map be shown to the witness. It's Brajkovici, Z5, Zenica/1 and 2, 3, scale 25.000, because I wish to put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please put it on the ELMO. Everyone will then be able to see it. Further re-examination by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In connection with Their Honours question about this Planina, or mountain, and the interpretation of the translators as to the meaning of "GG," I would like to -- you to tell me in which area all these units of the tactical group were active that were mentioned in the order attack of the 5th of June. Can you show us with the pointer where these units were?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want the initial deployment or during the 8th of June?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the 8th of June. You said first that Novo Selo was taken. That's what it says in the record. Can you show us where Novo Selo is.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'll mark it, if need be. The main forces went from the direction of Crni Vrh and Usice, from this mountain up here. And that's probably where the name, Planina, or mountain, comes from. Usice. And then there's Crni Vrh, which is not on this map. And they moved in this direction. That was the central axis. That's the axis along which they moved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The second day -- the second day, at around noon, the line reached by these main forces was on the Cukle -- on the line of Cukle and above Novo Selo. This is the line that they reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just show us where the most fierce fighting took place on that day. You said around 2000 hours at Vis [as interpreted] and when the flag was taken down at Strmac.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: The auxiliary forces had the task of getting up on this hill called Strmac from the direction of Kljaci and the other direction from Osojnici. These forces did not succeed on that day. They did not achieve the planned task and that's why the main forces were stopped at this line they had achieved because they were under fierce fire from their flanks. This activity had to be strengthened on the axis of the auxiliary forces because the main forces had been halted because there was resistance here and the main forces from their axis had the task of reaching this communication, and the most fierce fighting took place here in the area of Brajkovici and the village of Grahovcici, where there was resistance. And the longest and fiercest resistance was in the village of Vodine [phoen] and Strmac and around the village of Grahovcici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Did your forces have to go not direction of Guca Gora at all and where would this axis have been on your map?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: By no means. We never even considered it. What was important for us was to take this communication leading from Zenica via Han Bila and Novo Selo to liberate it, because this communication was very important for us, so that we could join up with these forces here and this communication. So the task was for the forces to reach Brajkovici and Grahovcici. And the furthest point was the village of Vrbice, the individuals of Vrbice which they were supposed to reach.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this map does not show parts of the Bijanska [phoen] Valley at all, where Guca Gora is.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Guca Gora is far away from here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So "GG" in your opinion can be no means refer to Guca Gora, as you've already said.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD IBRAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then thank you, sir. This concludes your testimony. We thank you for having answered all the questions put to you and for the indications -- the markings you made on the maps, which I think will be tendered into evidence. We'll deal with that in a minute. I wish you a good trip home and all the best in the position that you hold at the moment in the Ministry of Defence. I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now turn to the Defence to deal with the documents that you would like to tender. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we wish to tender the documents on the list of documents which are marked under Roman I, ID 0409 and the document under number VII, ID0393. As there is no translation into English, for purposes of identification until we get a translation, we ask for numbers to be given to document number 2, 1652; number 3, 1654; tab 4, 1655; tab 8, 1658; tab 9, 1659; tab 11, 1660; tab 12, 1662; and tab 22, 1673. We also wish to tender the two maps that the witness has marked and signed as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, the two maps that we have documents 1 and 7, and we have been asked to give definite numbers for these documents; and then we have documents 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 22 that should be marked for identification as we don't have the translations of these documents. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no objection to the documents going into evidence. There does seem to be a discrepancy, at least in the English transcript, between which precise documents they're asking to be marked for identification at this point in time. Perhaps if we could just get that clarified. It's 2, 3, 4, 8 -- or 5? 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12, and 22. We have no objection to those documents being marked for identification, nor to the other documents for which there is an English translation being admitted into evidence, as well as the two maps being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Registrar, you may take the floor to deal with this task.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We'll start with the maps. The first map shall be admitted; DH1991 will be the number. The scale of the map is 1 to 50.000. And "Zenica" can be seen at the bottom to the left. The second map will be admitted into evidence as DH1992. The scale of this map is 1 to 25.000. And we can see the name "Dusina" to the left at the bottom of the map. As far as the documents are concerned, the first document will be admitted into evidence. It used to be marked for identification, and the number is DH409. The English version will be DH409/E. The second document which will be admitted into evidence as an exhibit is DH393, formerly marked for identification. Its English version will be DH0393/E [as interpreted]. As far as the documents that will be marked for identification alone, the first one is DH1652. Then we have DH1654, DH1656, DH1658, DH1659, DH1660, DH1662, and finally DH1673. And that concludes the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Last Friday there was a DH document -- a Defence document, 1423, which was characterised as propaganda, dated the 1st of September, 1993. The Prosecution objected to admitting this document into evidence. After having deliberated, the Trial Chamber will admit this document into evidence. Mr. Registrar, document 1423 will be admitted into evidence. You may take the floor to confirm the fact.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hereby confirm that DH1423 will be admitted into evidence and the English version will be DH1424/E. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before we adjourn, I'd like to inform the parties that on Friday, the 11th of February, we will not be sitting, as the Judges have a Plenary Session. So on the 11th of February, 2005 there will be no hearing. The Judges will be meeting as of 9.30 and the meeting will probably go on throughout the day. As a result, there will be no hearing. What is the schedule for tomorrow? I will give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as we have already said, tomorrow we have a witness who is already here in The Hague. This is witness Serif Kadric. And he is the only witness for that day. On the following days, we have three more witnesses for two days because we estimate that their testimony will not be long, and we feel they can all be completed in two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, could I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will see everyone tomorrow at nine o'clock -- Yes, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I know we're after 7.00, but I wondered if I could just bring us back to where we started today on this translation issue again. I have now located the page where the witness who looked at the document testified about what was written in the document. It's page 14034 of the transcript of February -- of, sorry, Wednesday, 12 January 2005.
