Your Honours, I would request, with Your Honours' leave, that this document be provided to the Translation Unit by Mr. Registrar when he conveys the -- the new request to them to look at the matter. The reason being is that at the top of the page, when Mr. Ibrisimovic asked the witness about this document and he read out the section that has been focussed on in the Bosnian language - he read it from the original - and it was translated by the translation booths around us, and I quote from the page, as the Arabs - and the quote starts - "remained behind the 7th Muslim Brigade which has left the territory." So it was translated in court on the day as "remained behind" and not "were left behind" by the 7th Brigade. And I would request that that be conveyed to the Translation Unit, as it may be helpful to them in resolving this issue. Your Honours, on the rest of the page, the witness describes what -- what he intended when he wrote the document, but of course the translators have to look at what is -- is in the written document. And we would request that that be taken into account and that once we get the report from the Translation Unit, we can take the matter further from there, if necessary. Thank you for the -- the time over the time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Mundis, as far as this issue is concerned, you've heard what Mr. Dixon has just said. He would like CLSS to have the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would actually oppose that. We -- we have no objection to CLSS undertaking a re-look at the document, nor do we have any objection to CLSS listening again to the tapes of what the witness said and determining precisely what the witness said to determine if in fact the transcript accurately capture what is the witness said, but we don't believe, if -- if we're looking at -- to see what the document says, that should be independent of what the witness says the document says, in our respectful views. We have, again, no objection to both the tapes of the witness's testimony and the transcripts being looked at, nor do we have an objection to the document being re-looked at, but we don't believe that it would be appropriate for the person who is reviewing the document to have recourse to what the witness says about the document. We believe that the two pieces of evidence in fact need to be looked at separately, in terms of the -- the language used in the document and the language used by the witness in describing what's contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute I'll give you the floor in a minute. If I have understood the Prosecution's position correctly - but it's becoming increasingly complex - the Prosecution is saying that they don't object as a rule to having CLSS re-examining the text, the document, but the Prosecution would like those who do the work to do it without listening to the sound recording. It's necessary to disassociate these two elements. Is that what you are saying, Mr. Mundis? Are you saying that the translation service should have a look at the document but listen to the sound recording at the same time? What is it that you are trying to say exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. What we're saying is there's a document which CLSS has looked at and which the Defence would now like CLSS to look at again. We have no objection to CLSS looking at the document again, nor do we have an objection to CLSS listening to the tape of what the witness testified about last Wednesday and verifying if the transcript accurately captures what the witness said. What we do have an objection to is CLSS -- is in effect those two things being done simultaneously by the same person for the simple reason that when the witness was questioned about it, the phrasing of the question may have influenced what the witness said the document said. In other words, the two things need to be looked at independently. Let's get the document reviewed again, and let's have CLSS listen to the tape of what the witness actually said and make sure the transcript is accurate, but we don't believe it's the role of CLSS to be engaged in an -- in an exercise of interpreting what the witness says the document says, and then somehow revising the written document's translation to reflect what a witness said in court. Mr. President, that's the role of the Chamber in the event there's a discrepancy between what the witness says the document says and what the document as written in 1993 actually says. So we have no objection to trying to determine precisely what those two pieces of evidence say. What we do object to is someone in CLSS sitting down listening to the tape and then revising a written translation of a document based on what a witness testified about here in the courtroom. Those are two separate issues, as far as we're concerned, and it's for the Trial Chamber to determine what the document actually means, in terms of what the witness says it means and in terms of the written document. But the translation and interpretation issues should be kept separate, in our respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, to be brief, I wholly agree with my learned friend. What the witness said about what he intended the document to mean is evidence, and Your Honours can assess whether that evidence is probative or not. What we are here concerned about with is exactly what is written in the original written document. The reason why I wanted this page referred to the Translation Unit is that Mr. Ibrisimovic read out the Bosnian document, and somebody in the witness booth interpreted it as it was read out to be "remained behind the 7th Brigade." In other words, did not say "was left there by the 7th brigade." So we have one translator spontaneously translating it already. And that might be a helpful interpretation for the CLSS to take into account when they look at what the meaning is now. It was on the basis of -- of that translation in court by a translator that Mr. Ibrisimovic then explained that the Bosnian document, the way it is translated, on the written translation is incorrect, and that's why it was then referred to the Translation Unit. So I'm simply asking that that page be given to the Translation Unit because there is one spontaneous translation there already. It might help them in resolving this issue. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Dixon has drawn our attention to a fundamental issue. When the question was put in B/C/S by his colleague, it was interpreted into English. And we should at least know whether the interpretation does in fact correspond precisely to the question and the answer. So CLSS should also listen to the question put by Defence, to the interpretation into English, to the answer. So when I said that this was a complicated issue, I would in fact add that it is extremely complicated. Since it is so complicated, CLSS and all the relevant material, the question put by Defence counsel, the interpretation of the question into English, the response provided in B/C/S by the witness, the interpretation of the response provided by the witness, and the comparison of all these various elements, with the document, all of these elements should be examined and then we will be able to have a more precise idea of this complicated matter. This took 15 minutes of our time, and it might take up a few hours in the future, but let's hope that CLSS does what is necessary. As I was saying, we will resume our work tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
